proposed.sourceName: Darul Iftaa Mahmudiyyah (Lusaka, Zambia) — Fatwa #326 on Glycerine
proposed.paraphrase: A Hanafi darul-iftaa ruling that plant and synthetic glycerine is permissible while glycerine from an animal source is not permissible (the fat being generally from a non-halal animal), and that one should check the source and exercise caution when it is unverified — so the strict Hanafi practitioner avoids unverified glycerine.

proposed.sourceName: Islam Q&A — Fatwa 97541 (citing the Standing Committee for Issuing Fatwas)
proposed.paraphrase: Where haram content (pig-derived or improperly-slaughtered animal glycerine) is certain or strongly suspected, it is obligatory to avoid eating, drinking or using it; only a lawfully-slaughtered source (or genuine istihalah) makes it permissible — supporting strict avoidance of doubtful-source E422.

researcherNote: E422 seeded hanafiStrict = grade 4 (Questionable — widely avoided). The strict Hanafi position follows the cautious 'animal source not permissible / avoid when haram suspected' rulings; the more permissive 'assume-halal under hardship' Hanafi view (Darul Ifta Birmingham) maps to the general/lenient positions, not this one. Two independent tier-1 Sunni sources. APPROVED by owner 2026-07-01.
